Nothing compares the reviews banked in artifacts/review/ (each carries the reviewer's own reviewed_at, and README.md says every review is kept there) with the ledger's claude_review_run entries. Counterexample, run against the real gate code: in a scratch clone of d6f9ce0 I banked two SHIP reviews dated 2026-11-12T01:00:00Z and 2026-11-12T03:00:00Z. The second moved the first to history/, in a commit touching only artifacts/review/, which is what the final sequence commits after a review. The ledger kept its one 2026-11-12 entry. Yet two review runs on 2026-11-12 exceed the cap of 1 at the recorded share of 0.2. This is the path the 2026-11-11 overrun took. c605476 added make review-start, a step the main session has to remember, but no check, so a skipped review-start passes both gates again. README.md:185-186 ('any other overrun fails make budget') overstates this: make budget catches only overruns that were logged. A check the repository can already support: every banked review (every committed version of artifacts/review/latest.json, plus history/) needs its own claude_review_run entry at or before its reviewed_at, on the same or the previous UTC day. The current history passes this check: the two 2026-11-11 entries carry the reviews' own times, and the 2026-11-12 00:06:05 entry precedes this review.
